absent: PMU revision encoding and crystal frequency selection procedure are not shown.
GPIO lock ordering, interrupt context rules and interaction with bus layer locking are not shown.
Flash operation sequencing, timing, status polling and error recovery are not shown.
OTP programming, verification and protection enforcement semantics are not shown.
Clock mode transition steps and regulator voltage levels are not shown.
External interface timing calculation from nanoseconds, watchdog programming sequence and UART protocol details are not shown.
Wait count selection procedure and clock divider choice for PCMCIA, program and flash ports are not shown.
MIPS serial setup, flash window sizing and PCI host versus cardbus selection logic are not shown.

findings.text: Chipcommon AT flash control defines numeric operation codes for the two buffer flash engine. Main read is 0x07E8 and page read is 0x07D2 while status query is 0x01D7. Buffer writes use 0x0384 and 0x0387. Erase program uses 0x0283 and 0x0286 and plain program uses 0x0288 and 0x0289. Page erase is 0x0281 and block erase is 0x0250. Write erase program uses 0x0382 and 0x0385. Load uses 0x0253 and 0x0255, compare uses 0x0260 and 0x0261, and reprogram uses 0x0258 and 0x0259. Both buffer read codes are left without values.
AT flash status byte packs three fields. Ready is signalled by bit value 0x80 and mismatch by 0x40. Device identity occupies mask 0x38 and is positioned by a right shift of three.

One time programmable layout distinguishes hardware, software and customer identity regions through aliases to underlying hardware, software and identity protection markers. Signed word offsets place software limit at minus eight, customer base at zero and customer limit at plus eight, with boundary at minus four and hardware, software and customer signatures at minus three, minus two and minus one. Customer record order is identity at zero, package at one, function at two, reserved at three and limit at four. Expected signature constant is 0x578A and magic constant is 0x4E56.

Power subrecord stores a one byte revision followed by a four byte active crystal frequency measured in kilohertz. Enclosing chipcommon record stores in order a link to the underlying bus device, capability and status words, a two byte fast powerup delay, a GPIO spinlock, the embedded power subrecord, and two timing words giving ticks per millisecond and maximum timer span.

Chipcommon and external interface records each embed a spinlock dedicated to GPIO register access. Callers are expected to hold the owning core lock across GPIO read modify write sequences rather than relying on the bus layer for atomicity.

Chipcommon register access is offered as a small family that forwards single reads and writes to the underlying bus device at a caller supplied offset, plus three read modify write variants that preserve all bits outside the caller mask, force bits from a caller set, or combine mask then set. Availability is reported by testing whether the embedded device link is present.

Clock mode is a three value enumeration with slow first, fast second and dynamic third, implying zero through two in declaration order. Regulator voltage selector is a four value enumeration with power amplifier reference first at zero followed by three general voltage selectors in increasing order.

External interface maps caller supplied windows by fixed displacements. Memory window is identity, input output window adds one megabyte, configuration window adds two megabytes, configuration interface window adds eight megabytes and flash window adds twelve megabytes. The core exposes five GPIO output channels.

GPIO output and output enable addresses are computed from a channel index as a fixed base plus eight times the index. Out of range indexes are rejected at build time rather than at run time, so only indexes zero through four are valid.

External interface control space places control at zero with a UART enable low bit, and status at four with read only endian, external interrupt pin and GPIO interrupt pin low bits. PCMCIA configuration and three wait registers follow at 0x10 through 0x1C, program configuration and wait at 0x20 and 0x24, flash configuration and wait at 0x28 and 0x2C, watchdog at 0x40 and four clock controls at 0x44 through 0x50. GPIO input is at 0x60 with output and enable bases at 0x64 and 0x68, EJTAG enable at 0x90 and interrupt polarity and mask at 0x94 and 0x98.

External interface UART occupies eight registers spaced sixteen bytes apart from 0x300 for data through 0x370 for scratch, covering in order data, timer, FIFO control, line control, modem control, line status, modem status and scratch.

External configuration word packs enable at bit zero, a three bit mode field starting at bit one with flash as zero, synchronous as two and PCMCIA as four, a width select at bit four for eight versus sixteen bits, a byteswap at bit five, a two bit clock divider field starting at bit six with divide by two, three and four encodings, plus clock enable at bit eight and a synchronous only strobe at bit nine.

PCMCIA memory, attribute and input output timing registers each pack four wait counts with the lowest count in low bits and the upper three counts shifted by eight, sixteen and twenty four. Low field covers six bits while each upper field covers five bits within its byte.

Programmable and flash wait registers use the same four position packing with shifts of eight, sixteen and twenty four but with five bit coverage in every position. Programmable timing provides combined defaults of 0x0C in position zero, 0x0A00 in position one, 0x020000 in position two and 0x01000000 in position three.

Watchdog input clock is forty eight megahertz. Largest programmable interval is two to the twenty eighth power minus one ticks, with a millisecond ceiling derived by dividing that tick maximum by the clock rate in kilohertz.
When the external interface driver is present the record holds a link to the underlying bus device followed by a GPIO spinlock. When the driver is absent the record is empty and carries no fields.

Availability predicates for chipcommon and for the present external interface variant report true exactly when the embedded device link is present. The absent external interface variant always reports false without inspecting its argument.

Fallback external interface helpers perform no action. Clock control retrieval and nanosecond timing setup return without effect, watchdog setup returns zero, GPIO input and all masked GPIO output, enable, polarity and mask updates return zero, and serial initialization returns zero to indicate nominal success without touching hardware.

Serial port descriptor stores a register base, a clock speed, an interrupt number, a base baud rate and a register stride. Parallel flash descriptor stores presence, bus width and window base plus size. Serial flash descriptor stores presence, window base, block size, block count and total size plus an opaque private pointer. Full MIPS core record stores a device link, a serial port count and four embedded serial descriptors plus parallel flash and, when serial flash support is enabled, serial flash. The absent variant is empty.
Fallback MIPS helpers do nothing. Core initialization returns without effect and interrupt number lookup always yields zero regardless of the supplied device.

PCI core control at zero packs reset output enable and reset drive plus clock output enable and clock gate in low bits. Arbiter control at 0x10 selects internal or external arbitration and parks the idle bus on last requestor, on the 4710 agent or on external requestor zero or one. Interrupt status at 0x20 and mask at 0x24 each cover INTA, INTB, system error, parity error and power management, with error status cleared by writing. Mailbox at 0x28 raises per function interrupts for functions zero through three with two lines each.

Broadcast address at 0x50 uses a low byte mask with broadcast data at 0x54. GPIO input, output, enable and control occupy 0x60 through 0x6C on revision two and later. Three bus to PCI translations sit at 0x100 through 0x108 with high bit masks. Four PCI configuration windows sit at 0x400 through 0x700 on revision eight and later. Serial PROM shadow starts at 0x800 with two bytes per word over seventy two bytes.

Bus to PCI translation attributes encode memory as zero, input output as one and two configuration spaces as two and three, with prefetch, burst and memory read multiple modifiers plus a two bit read command mask selecting plain read, read line or read multiple on newer revisions. A board flag at 0x400 records that the board leaves PCI floating.
When the PCI driver is present the record holds a device link plus three one bit flags recording whether setup completed and whether host or cardbus mode is active. The absent variant is empty.

Fallback PCI helpers either do nothing or report absence. Core initialization returns without effect, device interrupt vector enable returns zero, while platform device setup and BIOS interrupt mapping both return a device absence error.

System address map places physical SDRAM at zero with a byteswapped alias at 0x10000000, host mode PCI memory and configuration windows at 0x08000000 and 0x0C000000, enumeration space from 0x18000000 to 0x18010000, second flash region at 0x1C000000 spanning thirty two megabytes, external interface base at 0x1F000000 with first flash at 0x1FC00000 spanning four megabytes, client mode PCI DMA at 0x40000000 spanning one gigabyte, PCI Express DMA low and high halves at zero and 0x80000000, plus derived UART and LED bases eight and nine megabytes above the external interface base.
Each routed header defines a single inclusion guard macro that prevents repeated inclusion within one translation unit.

Two buffer read operation codes are left undefined and must not be issued. OTP offsets include negative values that require signed arithmetic. GPIO index macros trap the build on out of range channels. Fallback helpers that return zero can mask missing hardware support and deferred error checks should treat absence explicitly.
